Architectural overview

Problem & architectural thesis

Automated due-diligence and compliance tools that summarize vendor pages with LLMs routinely hallucinate citations or silently omit sources they failed to fetch. Receipts and its extracted library Assay enforce verbatim byte-offset grounding and explicit 'not read' accounting.

Control flow

  1. ProposeSource Fetch & Model Proposer

    Fetches vendor pages alongside independent sources (SEC 10-K, NHTSA recalls, IIHS); an LLM proposes candidate claim-vs-source pairings.

  3. Deterministic GateAssay Byte-Offset Substring Gate

    Re-locates every quoted string verbatim in the fetched source bytes with exact offsets and discards unanchored quotes.

  5. Commit / RefuseAudited Ledger or Reasoned Refusal

    Writes structured ledger rows (disputed, unverified, context_unverified) and explicitly records blocked sources as 'not read'.

Key tradeoff & failure mode

Exact substring checks stop fabricated quotes but do not prove a quote is a fair reading—an earlier divergent Tesla row had to be removed after catching a truncated Wikipedia sentence. A frontier-model relation check denied 30/30 no-relation pairs but admitted only 2/5 real relations (left off by default); G2 (0/16 attempts) and Reddit could not be fetched and remain logged as 'not read'.

What it is

  • Receipts is a TypeScript pipeline that reads a vendor's pages and independent sources (including SEC filings, NHTSA and IIHS), lets a model propose which claims contradict which, and discards any quote a deterministic gate cannot re-find in the fetched bytes. #receipts-pipeline
  • Assay is the claim-audit constraint layer extracted from Receipts into a standalone TypeScript library (v0.1.0): corpus plus subject in, a ledger or a reasoned refusal out. #assay-library
